profile.campus: Culpeper, Virginia (former Terremark government-focused campus, acquired by Equinix 2016; Culpeper Technology Zone)
profile.address: 18155 Technology Drive, Building B, Culpeper, VA 22701
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's CU2 facility at 18155 Technology Drive, Building B, in Culpeper, Virginia, part of a former Terremark campus that Equinix acquired in 2016. Data Center Dynamics reported the campus was originally developed in 2008 to serve government customers, spans roughly 60 megawatts across multiple buildings, and sits within the Culpeper Technology Zone, a development area the county has deliberately managed to avoid sprawl. Equinix's own published specifications for CU2 describe a two story, precast concrete and steel frame building of 62,398 square feet (5,797 square meters), with a raised floor load capacity of 250 pounds per square foot and a slab capacity of 301 pounds per square foot, and a seismic design rating of D under the 2008 Universal Building Code. The page lists N+1 UPS redundancy, N+2 generator redundancy rated for 30 hours or more of runtime at full load, N+2 cooling redundancy, 120v/208v power distribution, and a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA. Fire protection combines double interlock pre-action suppression with both aspirated, HSSD or VESDA style, and non-aspirated detection, and security is listed as 24/7 with biometric entrance mantraps and video recording surveillance. Equinix lists nine certifications for CU2, HECVAT, HIPAA, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, ISO 9001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II, along with a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment. The page also lists sustainability features including wind and solar renewable energy credits sourced from multiple US regions and Canada, LED lighting, and hot and cold aisle containment. Equinix markets CU2 specifically as offering government grade capacity, a positioning Data Center Dynamics linked to the area's history serving federal customers, though Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for CU2 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Culpeper's data center growth is tied closely to Cold War era federal infrastructure. The nearby Mount Pony bunker, a Federal Reserve communications and records facility from the 1960s through the late 1990s, later became the Library of Congress's National Audio Visual Conservation Center rather than a data center, but the power and security infrastructure the Federal Reserve built to serve it helped seed early data center activity in the county, including a Swift financial network data center dating to the 1980s that Data Center Dynamics reported still operates today. Data Center Dynamics quoted an industry analyst describing Culpeper as proving a friendly area for data centers, citing abundant developable land, dual utility service from both Dominion Energy and Rappahannock Electric Cooperative, and its position roughly 55 miles south of the established Ashburn hub as a growth corridor positioned as complementary to, rather than competing with, Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. This entry treats Culpeper as an independent site from Ashburn and does not carry over any Ashburn specific campus figures, since Equinix's Culpeper and Washington DC metro pages are published and maintained separately and Equinix does not link the two areas together on either page.

reading.body:
Equinix CU2 is a 62,398 square foot building in Culpeper, Virginia, part of a former Terremark government-focused campus that Equinix acquired in 2016. The facility publishes no megawatt power capacity, so its scale in the campus and state cannot be compared to other sites using published specifications. The Culpeper campus as a whole spans roughly 60 megawatts across multiple buildings, but CU2's own draw is not disclosed.

CU2 holds nine certifications: HECVAT for government data handling, HIPAA for health information, ISO 22301 for business continuity, ISO 27001 for information security, ISO 9001 for quality management, NIST 800-53/FISMA High for federal systems, PCI DSS for payment systems, and SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II for audit compliance. The facility is designed for high-security and regulated workloads rather than public cloud or consumer services. A minimum cabinet density of 4 kilowatts per rack sets the lower bound for IT load, so the 62,398 square feet could house roughly 3,800 racks if fully deployed at that density, though this is an assumption about utilization, not a published figure.

Culpeper ranks 26th among Virginia's facilities by published megawatt capacity, but only 25 of Virginia's 330 mapped facilities publish power figures at all, so this ranking reflects disclosure rather than actual state prevalence. The county positions itself 55 miles south of Ashburn as a complementary growth corridor, not a competitor, with dual utility feeds from Dominion Energy and Rappahannock Electric Cooperative. CU2's unpublished capacity means it does not contribute to the grid constraint calculation for the state, leaving its role in Virginia's AI infrastructure unquantified.
